text: You've got a minor health issue, nothing urgent. You just want it fixed quickly, hoping for a simple walk-in or a fast slot today.
But calling the clinic, you hit the wall: "The next available appointment is in three days." Your heart sinks. Why can't you just show up?
You imagine an empty waiting room, or doctors sipping coffee, ignoring patients. It feels inefficient, like the system wants to make things harder for you.
The truth is, a doctor's time is a finite resource. Appointment slots are a clever system, designed in signal blue, to allocate that scarcity and prevent overwhelming surges.
Without them, everyone would rush in at once, creating endless, chaotic queues and burnt-out doctors. You pay with your wait, ensuring the system stays fair.
Now, when you book that future slot, you see past the frustration. You understand the invisible system keeping healthcare from utter collapse.
